title: Introduce local for 'this' is not very useful
body: **Version Used**: VS 15.7 **Steps to Reproduce**: 1. Move caret to `this` and press `Ctrl+.` ```C# sealed class C { readonly string s; public C(string s) { this.s = s; } } ``` **Expected Behavior**: Roslyn either doesn't offer to introduce a local for 'this' or it moves this refactoring to the bottom of the list. **Actual Behavior**: Roslyn thinks the most useful refactoring is storing 'this' in a local. Even if it's a struct, it's not very useful to show this refactoring, especially if it's a constructor.

answers: [{'timestamp': '2018-09-24 20:37:57+00:00', 'body': 'Why is this a bug?'}, {'timestamp': '2018-09-24 22:49:18+00:00', 'body': "Design Meeting Notes: Since `s` is `readonly`, it will cause an error. But more broadly, consider the following (explained in the comments). ```C# sealed class C { readonly string s; string t; C car = null; public C(string s) { this.s = s; // Introduce Local offered anywhere on `this`, with or without selection car.t = s; // Introduce Local only offered on `car` when it is selected } } ``` Let's treat `this` like `car`."}, {'timestamp': '2018-09-24 22:49:22+00:00', 'body': "@user is there a good use case for this that we've missed?"}]
